The queried species are outlined. For the pair cat, dog the lowest common ancestor is Carnivora (accent color, with its two edges); for cat, mouse it is Mammalia (teal, with the edges down to both). The card maps (cat, dog) to Carnivora and (cat, mouse) to Mammalia." width="100%"} Applies `lowest_common_ancestor()` to many pairs at once: for each pair, a common ancestor (each node counts as its own ancestor) with no descendant that is also a common ancestor. Use it to compute the most specific shared category for many pairs of terms in a taxonomy or ontology, or the merge base of many pairs of commits in a version history. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pairs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of `(u, v)` pairs (IDs or labels). If `None` (default), every pair of nodes, including each node with itself. [key]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable[[int], Any] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional function of a node ID used to choose among several lowest common ancestors: the one with the smallest `key` value is returned (ties go to the lowest node ID). If `None` (default), the choice of `lowest_common_ancestor()` is used. To get every lowest common ancestor, use `all_pairs_all_lowest_common_ancestors()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[tuple[int, int], int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v)` to the ID of a lowest common ancestor, for every pair that has a common ancestor (pairs without one are left out). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not a directed acyclic graph, is empty, or a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Ancestor sets are computed once per node and intersected per pair; within the common ancestors a lowest one is found by walking down while a successor stays common, as in NetworkX's `all_pairs_lowest_common_ancestor`. A pair can have several lowest common ancestors; this method returns the one `lowest_common_ancestor()` would, which may differ from NetworkX's choice. With `key=`, all lowest common ancestors of each pair are found first (see `all_pairs_all_lowest_common_ancestors()`) and the smallest by `key` is kept, as with the `key=` argument proposed in NetworkX pull request #7988. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#88abb1b6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["Mammalia", "Carnivora", "Rodentia", "cat", "dog", "mouse"]) tree.add_edges( [("Mammalia", "Carnivora"), ("Mammalia", "Rodentia"), ("Carnivora", "cat"), ("Carnivora", "dog"), ("Rodentia", "mouse")] ) found = tree.all_pairs_lowest_common_ancestor([("cat", "dog"), ("cat", "mouse")]) {tuple(tree.get_label_from_id(n) for n in pair): tree.get_label_from_id(a) for pair, a in found.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {('cat', 'dog'): 'Carnivora', ('cat', 'mouse'): 'Mammalia'} ``` ::: :::
